<1>A Nova Account is optional.</1> You can read this site, and use Nova products, without one. It exists so that one identity works across the Nova ecosystem instead of each product asking you to register separately.

<1>About this page.</1> This is an informational template written for the Nova website while the products are being built. It is not legal advice, and it has not been reviewed by a lawyer. It describes only what Nova actually does today — where a practice does not exist yet, the page says so instead of claiming one. The bracketed values are placeholders for details that have not been decided yet, and Nova itself is a brand direction still under review.

Nova products are built to run on your own machine. Unless a specific product says otherwise, you do not need an account to use them, and using them does not require you to send us anything.

Nova products are designed to keep your work on your own machine, in formats you can open elsewhere. Where a future product lets you publish or share something publicly, you would be giving us only the permission needed to host and display it for that purpose — and you would keep ownership of it.
Nova products are designed to run on your own hardware. Where a product works without a network connection, we intend to keep it that way.

Nova products can work alongside services we do not control. Atlas, for example, can be connected to an external model provider using a key you supply — that connection is optional, off by default, and governed by that provider's own terms.

Nova products read information about your own computer where a feature needs it — for example, checking available disk space, listing installed applications so you can open one, or choosing a suitable graphics setting.

When you choose to use a third-party service, its terms and privacy practices apply to what it does. We are not responsible for those services.

When you create one, we hold: your <1>email address</1>; a <2>scrypt hash of your password</2>, never the password itself, from which the password cannot be recovered; an optional <3>display name</3> if you give one; a list of your <4>active sessions</4>, so that signing out actually ends them; and, for as long as one is outstanding, a <5>hashed password-reset token</5>, which is deleted the moment it is used or expires. We also record <6>which Nova products the account has been used with</6> — a product name and a date, nothing about what you did there.
